subject: Renewal structure recast + graduated uptick path
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olivia Park <olivia.park@nexadata.com>, NexaData Procurement <procurement@nexadata.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal structure recast + graduated uptick path

Olivia / Nexa procurement team —

Thanks again for the conversation last week. Per our discussion I attached a refreshed quote and a short MAAP (attachment list below) that aligns to the new usage profile you shared. Two core asks from our side:

- Move to a 24-month committed term (co-term with your other vendor contract on 2029-01-01).
- Apply a graduated ramp schedule across the first 6 quarters to match your anticipated token growth (we keep unit price stable and surface consumption thresholds).

Highlights in the attached quote:
- Year 1: 40% of annual commit, with quarter-by-quarter release (Q1 10% / Q2 10% / Q3 10% / Q4 10%).
- Year 2: remaining 60% split evenly.
- Auto-renew: optional; default off. We included an auto-renew opt-in checkbox and a 60-day notification window.
- Can include a 30% burst cushion for unexpected usage (pay-as-you-go beyond cushion).

Open items I flagged for procurement: any internal approval windows we should align to, and whether you need the term to strictly co-term to 2029 or if a soft co-term with proration at invoice cut is acceptable.

Attachments: NexaData_MAAP_v2.pdf (MAAP with ramp tables)
             Redwood-Quote-NexaData-2027.xlsx (line-item pricing)

If that looks reasonable I can route a clean SOW + signature package through DocuSign for countersignature. Proposed next step: 30-minute alignment call Tues (4/6) to lock the cadence and get legal looped.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0191
https://redwoodinference.com

From: Olivia Park <olivia.park@nexadata.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: NexaData Procurement <procurement@nexadata.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 11:03:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal structure recast + graduated uptick path

Camila —

Appreciate the clear write-up and the attachments. A couple of clarifying questions from procurement before we take to budget owners: 

1) Auto-renew behavior: our finance team prefers auto-renew off (we want a reminder before renewal). The 60-day notification window is fine, but would you consider extending to 90 days for enterprise contracts?

2) Co-terming: our preferred path is strict co-term to 2029-01-01 (we do not want proration mid-cycle). If you require a proration model for the first year, we will need to see a pro forma showing monthly invoice impact.

3) Ramp schedule: the 6-quarter graduated ramp is logical. Can you confirm whether burst cushion billing is applied at the token rate or a blended rate? Also confirm whether the burst consumes committed units first or is billed separately.

4) Discounting: can you provide a one-time onboarding credit for the first quarter to offset initial usage overages during integration?

We can take a short call on 4/6 — 10am PT works for me.

Thanks,
Olivia Park
Head of Procurement | NexaData
olivia.park@nexadata.com | +1 206-555-0133

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 13:20:10 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Renewal structure recast + graduated uptick path — procurement questions

Karthik / Marissa —

Looping you both in. Procurement (Olivia) pushed back on two predictable items: strict co-term to 2029 (no proration) and extending the notification window to 90 days. They also asked about whether burst is billed at token rate vs blended and requested a one-time onboarding credit.

My read: we can accommodate strict co-term (we'll amortize on our side) if we keep the 24-mo term and lock the ramp schedule. Extending to 90 days is fine for Nexa (enterprise carveout) but that's outside standard ops — flagging as a leadership concession.

For burst: recommend we bill burst at the committed per-token rate for simplicity, and bill consumption beyond cushion as pay-as-you-go at the same per-token price but without being reconciled against the commit. This keeps the math clean and reduces disputes.

Onboarding credit: propose a one-time $25k credit applied in Q1 invoice to cover integration overage risk. If legal needs it as a separate credit memo, we can do that.

Can we confirm margin impact and signoff thresholds? If you approve, I'll update the quote and send back to Olivia with a DocuSign link.

Thanks,
Camila

Thanks for the questions — appreciate the precision. We've updated the package based on your asks. Summary of changes (attached updated quote and MAAP):

- Co-term: We confirm strict co-term to 2029-01-01. Redwood will prorate internal accounting to align the initial partial period so NexaData invoices are fixed to the co-term boundary (no mid-cycle proration on your invoices).
- Notification window: extended to 90 days for this enterprise arrangement.
- Burst billing: burst consumption will be billed at the committed per-token rate; anything above the burst cushion is billed as overage at the same per-token rate on pay-as-you-go terms.
- Onboarding credit: one-time $25,000 credit applied to the Q1 invoice (credit memo will be attached to the SOW).

I've attached: Redwood-Quote-NexaData-2027_v2.xlsx and NexaData_MAAP_v3.pdf (updated ramp table and sample invoice layout).
